record.original_question: Characterize all multiplier sequences {gamma_k}_{k>=0} that admit a C_k-representation: there exist functions phi, Phi in L-P+ and real parameters s,t such that gamma_k = sum_{j=0}^k binom(k,j) B_j^phi(t) B_{k-j}^Phi(s), where B_m^phi(u)=sum_{r=0}^m binom(m,r)(1-u)^r a_{m-r} u^{m-r} when phi(x)=sum_{m>=0} a_m x^m/m!.

evidence.quote: Definition 31. Let gamma_k in R for k = 0, 1, 2, .... We say that the sequence {gamma_k}_0^infinity has a C_k-representation, if there exist functions phi, Phi in L - P+ and s, t in R such that gamma_k = C_k^{phi,Phi}(t, s) for all k in N_0, where C_k^{phi,Phi}(t, s) is as defined in equation (4.2).
Problem 44. Characterize all multiplier sequences which have a C_k-representation.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^+$ denote the Laguerre–Pólya class of type I consisting of real entire functions that are locally uniform limits of real polynomials having only real non-positive zeros (equivalently, functions of the form $C x^n e^{\sigma x}\prod_k(1+\alpha_k x)$ with $C\in\mathbb{R}$, $n\in\mathbb{N}_0$, $\sigma\ge 0$, $\alpha_k\ge 0$, $\sum\alpha_k<\infty$).

For $\varphi\in\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^+$ with Taylor expansion $\varphi(x)=\sum_{m\ge 0} a_m \frac{x^m}{m!}$, define the polynomials
$$B_m^{\varphi}(u)=\sum_{r=0}^{m}\binom{m}{r}(1-u)^r\, a_{m-r}\, u^{\,m-r},\qquad m\in\mathbb{N}_0.$$

For $\varphi,\Phi\in\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^+$ and $s,t\in\mathbb{R}$ set
$$C_k^{\varphi,\Phi}(t,s)=\sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{k}{j} B_j^{\varphi}(t)\, B_{k-j}^{\Phi}(s),\qquad k\in\mathbb{N}_0.$$

A real sequence $\{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is called a multiplier sequence if the linear operator $T:\mathbb{R}[x]\to\mathbb{R}[x]$ defined by $T[x^k]=\gamma_k x^k$ maps every real polynomial with only real zeros to a real polynomial with only real zeros (or to the zero polynomial).

A multiplier sequence $\{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ is said to admit a $C_k$-representation if there exist $\varphi,\Phi\in\mathcal{L\text{-}P}^+$ and $s,t\in\mathbb{R}$ such that
$$\gamma_k=C_k^{\varphi,\Phi}(t,s)\quad\text{for all } k\in\mathbb{N}_0.$$

Problem: Characterize all multiplier sequences $\{\gamma_k\}_{k\ge 0}$ that admit a $C_k$-representation.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any subsequent paper resolving the characterization of multiplier sequences admitting a $C_k$-representation. The literature on multiplier sequences and the Laguerre–Pólya class continues to develop (e.g., results on Laguerre/Hermite multiplier sequences and convolution operators preserving total positivity), but no source directly addressing this specific characterization problem was located.

status_evidence.title: Laguerre Multiplier Sequences and Sector Properties of Entire Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies multiplier sequences and the Laguerre-Pólya class but does not characterize C_k-representations.
status_evidence.claim: No characterization of C_k-representations is given in available related work.

status_evidence.title: Convolution operators preserving the set of totally positive sequences
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on operators related to multiplier sequences and total positivity.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature does not appear to resolve the C_k-representation problem.
